parts: create some facebook posts that i can put into medspa groups that advertise our new program, but not sound so spammy or saley

Because you are posting inside **med spa owner groups**, the key is to make the post feel like **peer advice from someone in the industry**, not an ad. The tone should feel like you are sharing something you discovered working with clinics.

Here are **several styles** you can rotate so you don't look promotional. All of these position you as a helpful insider.

---

### Post Option 1: “Observation” Post
This style works really well in Facebook groups.

**Post:**

One thing we’ve noticed working with med spas over the last year…

Most clinics don’t actually have a lead problem.

They have a **system problem.**

Leads come in, but then somewhere along the way things start leaking:
• no-shows  
• slow follow up  
• consultations that stall  
• front desk overwhelmed  
• patients who never come back

When those pieces aren’t working together, marketing ends up feeling random and expensive.

We’ve been building something called the **Luxora Growth Engine** that focuses on fixing the systems inside the clinic first, not just running ads.

Curious if anyone else has run into this in their practice? What do you feel like breaks down most after a lead comes in?

---

### Post Option 2: “Industry Discussion”
This creates engagement first.

**Post:**

Quick question for other med spa owners…

If you had to choose, what’s the **hardest part of growth right now?**

A) Getting quality leads  
B) Getting patients to actually show up  
C) Converting consultations  
D) Getting patients to come back consistently

We’ve been helping clinics fix these through a system we built that focuses on three things:

• smarter patient acquisition  
• automated booking & follow up  
• staff training around consultations

But I’m curious what everyone else is seeing right now.

---

### Post Option 3: “Story Post”
Story based posts feel the least salesy.

**Post:**

A med spa owner told me something last week that stuck with me.

She said:  
“We get leads… but growth still feels unpredictable.”

When we looked inside her clinic, we found a few things happening:

• inquiries sitting for hours before reply  
• no deposit to secure appointments  
• inconsistent consultation flow  
• zero structured follow up

None of that is a marketing problem.

It’s a **system problem.**

Once we installed the systems, the same leads started converting.

That’s actually why we created the **Luxora Growth Engine**. It focuses on fixing the entire growth system, not just marketing.

Curious if other clinics have experienced the same thing?

---

### Post Option 4: “Free Value Post”
Great if you want to softly introduce your blueprint.

**Post:**

I’ve been doing something interesting for a few clinics lately.

We’ve been building **data-driven market blueprints** for their med spa before touching their marketing.

It shows:
• where their best patients actually come from  
• what services are driving the highest revenue  
• where their booking system is leaking  
• and where growth is being lost

Honestly it’s been eye opening for a lot of owners.

If anyone wants one done for their clinic, I’m happy to take a look and build one.

No pitch. I just like digging into the numbers.

---

### Post Option 5: “Authority Post”
This positions Luxora without sounding like an ad.

**Post:**

One of the biggest myths in this industry is that growth comes from **more leads.**

After working with a lot of clinics, we’ve learned something different.

Growth usually comes from fixing these five things:

1. Patient acquisition strategy  
2. Booking friction  
3. Consultation flow  
4. Staff confidence in guiding patients  
5. Retention systems

When those are aligned, marketing works dramatically better.

That’s actually the framework behind what we built called the **Luxora Growth Engine**.

Would love to hear what other owners are seeing in their clinics right now.

---

### Bonus Tip (Very Important)

In Facebook groups, **do NOT include links in the first post**.

Instead:

1. Post the discussion
2. Let people comment
3. Then reply with something like:

> Happy to send the blueprint if you want me to take a look at your clinic.

This dramatically increases responses and avoids admins deleting it.

---

If you want, I can also give you **5 “comment replies”** you can use when people engage so it **naturally moves them into a DM or consult without sounding salesy**. That’s where most of the conversions actually happen.
